public_rationale: Marcus expressly qualified this assertion with 'so far as I know.' Scoring whether any CEO had ever publicly explained the singularity would remove that qualification and answer a different question. The supplied text and search do not establish his knowledge at publication. The claim therefore cannot fairly receive a truth verdict as worded under these rules.
limitations: This decision does not establish whether the CEOs had publicly defined the singularity.
It does not infer that Marcus's qualification was sincere or insincere.

our_interpretation: The qualification limits the assertion to Marcus's knowledge when he published the post on July 28, 2026.
The surrounding discussion concerns whether the referenced CEOs explained what they meant by their claims about the singularity.
Finding a public definition would not by itself establish that Marcus knew of it or that it explained the meaning of the claims he was discussing.
No unconditional assertion about the entire public record is substituted for the qualified statement.
criteria.support_condition: Evidence would need to establish that Marcus knew of no relevant definition when he published the post. His assertion alone and a search finding no definitions would not independently establish this.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous evidence would need to establish that Marcus already knew of a definition explaining a referenced CEO's meaning in the claims under discussion. An older explanation, without evidence of his awareness and its relevance, would not suffice.
